standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of a birational morphism: there are dense open subschemes over which the morphism induces an isomorphism, which allows reducing to an affine irreducible case
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies assuming both schemes affine and irreducible and gives the isomorphism of local rings at the generic points.

standard_prerequisites.name: The generic point of an irreducible component corresponds to a minimal prime, and there is a unique minimal prime of the source lying over the minimal prime of the target in the birational situation
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the primes whose local rings are compared.

standard_prerequisites.name: An element of a local ring whose image in the residue field is zero up to the maximal ideal, and the comparison of the localized ring with the local ring at a minimal prime
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the localized source ring is a local ring of dimension zero and hence equal to the local ring at the minimal prime.

core_obligations: Reduce to the affine irreducible case: assume the target affine and irreducible, note the source is then irreducible as well, observe that proving the statement for any nonempty affine open of the source suffices, and hence assume the source affine too (proof lines 13245-13250).

Translate to primes: let the chosen point correspond to the minimal prime of the target coordinate ring; by birationality the source coordinate ring has a unique minimal prime lying over it and the local rings at those primes are isomorphic (proof lines 13250-13252).

Conclude: the image of the source ring localized at the target prime inside the residue field is all of that residue field, so the extension of the minimal prime becomes a maximal ideal and is at the same time the unique minimal prime, forcing the localized source ring to have exactly one prime and to coincide with the local ring at the minimal prime; since that localized ring is the base change appearing in the statement, the base change is an isomorphism (proof lines 13252-13260).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to affine irreducible schemes and to the local situation at the minimal primes (proof lines 13245-13252).

Use that the localized source ring has a unique prime, namely the extension of the minimal prime, to identify it with the local ring at that minimal prime and hence with the base change (proof lines 13252-13260).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a birational morphism between schemes with finitely many irreducible components, the base change to the local ring at a generic point of the target is an isomorphism (statement lines 13236-13243). The counted proof is a short but genuine commutative algebra reduction: it passes to an affine irreducible situation, identifies the generic point with a minimal prime, uses birationality to know that the corresponding local rings are isomorphic and that there is a unique minimal prime upstairs, and then shows that the localized source ring has exactly one prime by exhibiting the extension of the minimal prime as both minimal and maximal, from which the identification with the base change follows (proof lines 13245-13260). It is H2: the argument is carried out in the counted span and its inputs are the standard dictionary between points, minimal primes and local rings.
